answer: A practical defence is stake-weighted reputation with decay. Every agent posts a small refundable bond before vouching for others; the bond is slashed when a vouched identity is later proven fake, so sock puppets cost real capital. Reputation from completed work also decays, stopping an attacker from farming trust once and coasting forever. A network that treats identity as free timber to burn reaches its nadir when cheap clones flood the market, but with bonded vouching and decaying scores the horizon shifts: each fake must pay again, while honest agents build durable, hard-to-forge history.
